# package isotp

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-canbus/isotp"
```

Package isotp implements ISO 15765-2 (ISO-TP), the transport protocol that carries messages of up to 4095 bytes (or 4 GiB with the escape sequence) over CAN frames, in userspace on top of a canbus.Bus.

It supports normal addressing (also with 29-bit identifiers, as normal fixed addressing uses them), extended addressing (target address in the first payload byte) and mixed addressing (address extension in the first byte); single, first, consecutive and flow control frames; block size and STmin, including the 100–900 µs values; flow control WAIT with a limit and OVERFLOW; sequence number wrap-around; the N\_Bs and N\_Cr timeouts; padding; classical CAN and CAN FD frames (TX\_DL 8 to 64, single frame escape) and the first frame escape for messages larger than 4095 bytes. Message sizes are bounded by Config.MaxMessageSize.

The Linux kernel's ISO-TP sockets offer the same with the same Config: see socketcan.DialISOTP. Both implement [Endpoint](#type-endpoint).

ISO 15765-2 is not publicly available; this implementation follows public descriptions and is tested against independent implementations (the Linux kernel and python-can-isotp). It makes no conformance claim.

## Variables

```go
var (
	// ErrTimeout reports a peer that did not send a flow control frame in
	// time (N_Bs) or a consecutive frame in time (N_Cr).
	ErrTimeout = errors.New("isotp: timeout")
	// ErrOverflow reports a receiver that answered OVERFLOW: the message
	// is larger than it accepts.
	ErrOverflow = errors.New("isotp: receiver overflow")
	// ErrWaitLimit reports more consecutive WAIT flow controls than
	// Config.MaxWait.
	ErrWaitLimit = errors.New("isotp: too many flow control WAIT frames")
	// ErrSequence reports a consecutive frame with a wrong sequence
	// number; the message being received is dropped.
	ErrSequence = errors.New("isotp: wrong sequence number")
	// ErrTooLarge reports a message larger than Config.MaxMessageSize or
	// than the protocol allows.
	ErrTooLarge = errors.New("isotp: message too large")
	// ErrInterrupted reports a reception that a new single or first
	// frame replaced.
	ErrInterrupted = errors.New("isotp: reception interrupted by a new message")
	// ErrProtocol reports an invalid flow control frame.
	ErrProtocol = errors.New("isotp: protocol error")
)
```

Errors. They are wrapped with detail; test with errors.Is.

## Functions

### func DecodeSTmin

```go
func DecodeSTmin(b byte) time.Duration
```

DecodeSTmin converts an STmin byte to a duration. Reserved values mean 127 ms, as ISO 15765-2 requires of a sender.

### func EncodeSTmin

```go
func EncodeSTmin(d time.Duration) (byte, error)
```

EncodeSTmin is the STmin byte of a duration, for kernel sockets and tools.

### type Config

```go
type Config struct {
	// TxID is the identifier of frames this side sends, RxID that of the
	// frames it receives. ExtendedIDs makes both 29-bit.
	TxID, RxID  canbus.ID
	ExtendedIDs bool

	// Addressing mode; TxAddress is the first byte of frames sent and
	// RxAddress the first byte expected in frames received (extended
	// and mixed addressing).
	Addressing           Addressing
	TxAddress, RxAddress byte

	// FD sends CAN FD frames of up to TxDL bytes (8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32,
	// 48 or 64; default 64 with FD, 8 without). BRS sets bit rate
	// switching on them.
	FD   bool
	TxDL int
	BRS  bool

	// BlockSize and STmin are sent in the flow control frames of this
	// receiver: how many consecutive frames the sender may send before
	// the next flow control (0: all), and the minimum gap between them
	// (0 to 127 ms, or 100 µs steps from 100 to 900 µs).
	BlockSize uint8
	STmin     time.Duration
	// ForceTxSTmin, when set, replaces the STmin the peer asks for.
	ForceTxSTmin *time.Duration

	// Padding pads every frame to its full length (8 bytes, or the CAN
	// FD length) with PadByte (default 0xCC). CAN FD frames are always
	// padded to a valid CAN FD length.
	Padding bool
	PadByte *byte

	// TimeoutBs is N_Bs, the wait for a flow control frame (default 1 s);
	// TimeoutCr is N_Cr, the wait for a consecutive frame (default 1 s).
	TimeoutBs, TimeoutCr time.Duration
	// MaxWait is the number of WAIT flow controls accepted in a row
	// (WFTmax; default 10).
	MaxWait int
	// MaxMessageSize bounds received and sent messages (default 4095;
	// up to 1<<32−1 with the first frame escape). A larger first frame
	// is answered with OVERFLOW.
	MaxMessageSize int
	// FlowControlDelay (N_Br) waits this long before each flow control
	// frame of this receiver (default 0). On a virtual interface the Linux
	// kernel's ISO-TP sender can miss a flow control that answers a block
	// faster than the kernel processes the echo of its own last frame
	// (it enters its wait state only then, net/can/isotp.c): a few hundred
	// microseconds avoid that race. Real buses need no delay.
	FlowControlDelay time.Duration
	// ListenOnly reassembles messages without ever transmitting: no flow
	// control is sent and Send fails (as the kernel's
	// CAN_ISOTP_LISTEN_MODE). Use it to monitor a transfer between two
	// other nodes; it then sees the messages sent on RxID.
	ListenOnly bool
	// SendFlowWait makes this receiver answer the first frame with this
	// many WAIT flow controls before CTS (for tests of peers).
	SendFlowWait int
	// QueueSize is the number of received messages (and errors) held
	// for Receive (default 16).
	QueueSize int

	Logger  *slog.Logger
	Metrics Metrics
}
```

Config configures an ISO-TP connection. The same Config works for the userspace [Conn](#type-conn) and the kernel socket.

### type Conn

```go
type Conn struct {

	// 1 with extended or mixed addressing

	// serializes Send

	// Reception state, owned by the reader goroutine.

}
```

Conn is a userspace ISO-TP connection on a [canbus.Bus](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#Bus). Send may be called from several goroutines (calls are serialized), Receive from one at a time. The connection does not own the bus.

#### func Dial

```go
func Dial(bus *canbus.Bus, cfg Config) (*Conn, error)
```

Dial starts an ISO-TP connection on bus: it subscribes to RxID and starts the goroutine that receives frames.

#### func (Conn) Close

```go
func (c *Conn) Close() error
```

Close stops the connection. Blocked Send and Receive calls return [canbus.ErrClosed](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canbus#ErrClosed).

#### func (Conn) Receive

```go
func (c *Conn) Receive(ctx context.Context) ([]byte, error)
```

Receive returns the next complete message, or a reception error (ErrTimeout for N\_Cr, ErrSequence, ErrInterrupted) as the kernel's ISO-TP sockets report them.

#### func (Conn) Send

```go
func (c *Conn) Send(ctx context.Context, payload []byte) error
```

Send transmits one message and returns when its last frame was sent.

Endpoint is an ISO-TP connection: the userspace [Conn](#type-conn) or a kernel socket.

### type Metrics

```go
type Metrics interface {
	OnMessageSent(size int, d time.Duration)
	OnMessageReceived(size int, d time.Duration)

}
```

Metrics observes an ISO-TP connection. Methods must be safe for concurrent use and must not block. Embed [NopMetrics](#type-nopmetrics).
